questions.prompt: What should this optimization target first?
questions.description: The real benchmark shows recalculateSchedule is around 19 ms, while calculateMppFields is around 1.7 s for the reported cronograma.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Optimize calculateMppFields first, especially repeated scans and per-task derived maps in the MPP calculation engine. Leave CPM incremental recalculation for later unless benchmarks still show UI latency.

questions.prompt: What performance result should count as success?
questions.description: This decides how aggressive the implementation needs to be.
questions.recommendedAnswer: For the provided preconstruction .mpp, reduce calculateMppFields from about 1.7 s to under 250 ms locally, while keeping recalculateSchedule under 50 ms.

questions.prompt: Which behavior must be preserved exactly?
questions.description: These are the regression boundaries for the optimization.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Preserve schedule dates, dependencies, critical path fields, MPP calculated columns, resource and assignment derived fields, autosave payload shape, undo/redo behavior, and project reload persistence.

questions.description: This controls how much architecture change is allowed.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Allow local indexes, precomputed per-task context, dependency lookup maps, assignment lookup maps, and focused memoization inside the existing calculation pipeline. Avoid a new parallel scheduling model.

questions.prompt: What verification should be required before calling it done?
questions.description: The app runs in Docker, and the issue is visible in runtime.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Run focused unit tests for scheduling and MPP calculations, add a benchmark/performance test for the real preconstruction .mpp path or a representative fixture, run lint/build, and verify the Docker-served app reflects the change.
